frontMatter.title: HomeLab
frontMatter.description: A production-grade home server running a suite of self-hosted services behind a private VPN mesh. Designed around privacy, data ownership, and developer productivity — with zero reliance on third-party cloud subscriptions for core workflows.

pageProps.markdown: A production-grade home server running a suite of self-hosted services behind a private VPN mesh. Designed around privacy, data ownership, and developer productivity — with zero reliance on third-party cloud subscriptions for core workflows. --- ## Architecture Overview Most services are containerized with **Docker** and managed through **Portainer**. Secure remote access is handled by a **Tailscale** mesh VPN, with **Caddy** acting as a reverse proxy for HTTPS routing to each service. A unified **Homepage** dashboard provides a single pane of glass across the entire stack. AI inference workloads run via **Ollama** and **llama.cpp**, surfaced through **Open WebUI** as a unified chat and tooling interface. **Click for full size** · the **[standalone page](design/homelab-diagram.html)** follows your light/dark setting Read the diagram as containment. The **Tailscale mesh** is the outer boundary — the laptop, the phone and the server all sit inside one private WireGuard network, so a name like `photos.local` only resolves for a device already on the tailnet. There is no public DNS record and no forwarded port. **Caddy** is drawn straddling that boundary because that is the job it does: it is the single point where a request crosses from the mesh into the machine. It resolves the `.local` hostname to a container port and terminates TLS with a tailnet-issued certificate. Technically it runs on the box like everything else, but it belongs to the edge, not to the stack behind it. Inside sits the **Docker** runtime. **Portainer** is drawn above everything else in it because it runs and administers every Compose stack below — it is the control plane, not a destination. **Homepage** sits under it as a pure display layer: it links out to each service but nothing routes *through* it. Below that are the five containerised apps and the AI stack. **ComfyUI** is the one service Docker does not host — it runs directly on the host for GPU access, which is why it is drawn outside the runtime with a dashed border. Caddy still routes `ai.local` to it. Underneath the AI stack sits the **Obsidian vault**, serving two readers: it is chunked and embedded for RAG retrieval, and read verbatim by the coding agents as operating instructions. Only two paths leave the lab — ProtonVPN egress and Claude Code's call to the Anthropic API. > Diagrams are generated, not drawn. Source in > [`tools/diagram/`](tools/diagram/); rebuild with `make -C tools/diagram diagram`. --- ## Networking ### Tailscale A WireGuard-based mesh VPN that connects all devices — laptop, phone, and server — into a single private network without opening any ports on the host router. Each service is accessible from anywhere as if on a local network. - **Tailscale HTTPS Serve** — provisions valid TLS certificates for Tailscale nodes, enabling HTTPS for all internal services without a public domain or manual certificate management. ### Caddy A modern reverse proxy used to route HTTPS traffic to each containerized service by hostname. Caddy handles automatic certificate renewal and TLS termination, keeping all service endpoints secured with minimal configuration. ### ProtonVPN Outbound VPN for general internet traffic from the host. Ensures the server's external IP is masked for privacy on egress connections. It is egress-only and never fronts inbound traffic. --- ## AI Stack The homelab runs a fully local AI stack — no external API keys required for core inference. Models are served through two backends depending on use case, both exposed to **Open WebUI** as a unified interface. ### 🤖 Open WebUI **Self-hosted AI chat interface** deployed via Docker. Open WebUI acts as the primary frontend for all local LLM interaction, connecting to multiple inference backends simultaneously: - **Ollama API** — serves quantized open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, etc.) with hardware-accelerated local inference. Used for general chat, coding assistants, and tool-calling workflows. - **llama.cpp API** — serves GGUF-format models with fine-grained control over context length, quantization level, and memory allocation. Used when direct model configuration is required beyond what Ollama exposes. - **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)** — Open WebUI's built-in RAG pipeline is connected to a local document store ingested from the Obsidian vault. Markdown notes, references, and processed documents are chunked, embedded, and stored in a vector database, enabling context-aware queries against personal knowledge directly from the chat interface. ### 🔍 Vane *(formerly Perplexica)* **Self-hosted AI-powered search engine** deployed via Docker. Vane is an open-source Perplexity alternative that combines web search with LLM synthesis — retrieving live search results and passing them through a local Ollama model to generate cited, summarized answers. Keeps AI-assisted web research entirely local and private. ### 💻 OpenCode **Terminal-based AI coding assistant** integrated with the local Ollama API. OpenCode provides an interactive CLI coding agent — capable of reading, editing, and reasoning about codebases — using locally served models rather than cloud APIs. Used as a self-hosted alternative to cloud coding assistants for private repository work. ### 🗣 Pi **Conversational AI assistant** integrated with Ollama. Pi provides a persistent, persona-driven chat interface backed by a locally running model, used for open-ended reasoning, research assistance, and ideation workflows within the homelab. ### 🎨 ComfyUI **Node-based Stable Diffusion interface** for local AI image generation. Runs directly on the host rather than in a container, giving it direct GPU access without virtualization overhead. ComfyUI's graph-based workflow system enables reproducible, version-controlled generation pipelines stored as JSON. --- ## Knowledge Management ### 🧠 Obsidian **Primary second brain and knowledge management system** — not a hosted service, but a central node in the homelab's information architecture. The Obsidian vault serves multiple roles: - **Personal knowledge base** — notes, research, references, and project documentation are stored as plain Markdown files, version-controlled via Gitea through the Obsidian Git plugin. - **AI retrieval corpus** — vault content is ingested into Open WebUI's RAG pipeline, making personal notes and accumulated knowledge queryable through local LLMs. This creates a closed loop where research done in Obsidian becomes context for AI-assisted workflows. - **Skills and workflow storage** — structured notes define repeatable processes, prompt templates, and domain knowledge used to condition model behavior in AI pipelines. - **Library and reading tracker** — PDFs and academic papers are stored in an `Attachments/` directory with corresponding Markdown pages tracking reading progress, highlights, quotes, and author metadata under a unified `Library/` structure. Vault backups are automated via Obsidian Git, committing and pushing to a private Gitea repository on a configurable schedule — providing full version history for all notes. --- ## Services ### 🖼 Immich **Self-hosted photo and video backup** — a drop-in replacement for Google Photos. Deployed via Docker Compose, Immich provides automatic mobile backups, facial recognition, album management, and a web UI. All media stays on-premises with no third-party access. ### 🗂 Gitea **Self-hosted Git service** — a lightweight alternative to GitHub. Used as the primary remote for all personal and homelab repositories, with full support for webhooks, issues, and access tokens. - Integrated with **Obsidian Git** for automated Obsidian vault backups and version control, pushing vault snapshots to a private Gitea repo on a configurable schedule. ### 🔖 Karakeep **Self-hosted bookmark and link archive manager**. Captures web pages with full-page screenshots and readable content, organized by collection and tags. Replaces browser bookmarks and cloud bookmark services, keeping a permanent, searchable archive of saved links. ### 📚 Calibre-Web **Self-hosted digital library server** for ebooks. Provides a clean reader UI, reading progress tracking, and OPDS support, browsing an existing Calibre library. Serves the local ebook collection over the Tailscale network to any device. ### 🐳 Portainer **Docker management UI** for the entire container stack. Provides a visual interface for managing containers, images, volumes, networks, and Docker Compose stacks — used for deployment, monitoring, and quick log inspection. ### 🏠 Homepage **Unified service dashboard** (gethomepage.dev) configured as the homelab's entry point. Aggregates live status, stats, and quick links for every running service. Widgets pull live data directly from service APIs — container counts from Portainer, photo counts from Immich, repo counts from Gitea, etc. --- ## Backup Strategy | Data | Method | |---|---| | Obsidian vault | Gitea (via Obsidian Git, automated commits) | | System | Scheduled local snapshots to external disk | | Photos | Immich (on-prem) + cloud photo sync (redundancy) | | Documents / config | Encrypted cloud drive (offsite copy) | A layered approach: local snapshots for fast recovery, Gitea for code and notes version history, and an offsite copy for critical documents and photos. --- ## Key Design Decisions **A small-form-factor host** — A low-power machine with a unified memory architecture is well-suited to running 24/7, and its integrated GPU is enough for local inference and image generation without a discrete card. **Tailscale over self-managed WireGuard** — Eliminates the operational complexity of key distribution and NAT traversal while retaining WireGuard's performance and security model. No ports exposed to the public internet. **Caddy over NGINX** — Automatic HTTPS, minimal configuration surface, and native support for Tailscale HTTPS certificates reduces the maintenance burden for TLS across services. **Gitea over GitHub for private repos** — Full control over repository data and access, with no dependency on an external service for personal and homelab infrastructure code.
